Embryonic stem cells only contain mitochondrial DNA without nuclear chromosomes
Adult stem cells carry zero risk of immunological rejection in allogeneic patients
Embryonic stem cells produce higher levels of carbon dioxide than somatic cells
Induced pluripotent stem cells can only be sourced from cloned primates
Embryonic stem cells lack nitrogenous bases in their genome
explanation: The core ethical controversy centers on the moral status of the human embryo and its destruction during the harvesting of the inner cell mass.

question: Which genetic mechanism best explains why two dark-skinned parents can have children with varying shades of skin colour, ranging from light brown to very dark brown?
correct_answer: Polygenic inheritance with additive effects from multiple gene loci and independent assortment
wrong_answers_pool: Complete dominance at a single autosomal gene locus
A single sex-linked recessive allele on the X chromosome
Incomplete dominance at a single gene locus with only three phenotypes
Mitochondrial mutations inherited strictly from the mother
Environmental tanning without any genetic contribution
Epistatic masking of melanin by ribosomal RNA
explanation: Skin pigmentation in humans is controlled by at least three or more polygenes (e.g. A, B, C) where each dominant allele contributes incrementally to melanin synthesis.

question: Pedigree analysis problem 1: A male with red-green colour blindness (XrY) and a female with normal vision whose father was colour-blind (XRXr) have children. What proportion of their total offspring is expected to be colour-blind?
correct_answer: 50% (half of all offspring: 50% of daughters and 50% of sons)
explanation: Cross: XrY x XRXr -> Daughters: 1 XRXr (carrier), 1 XrXr (colour-blind); Sons: 1 XRY (normal), 1 XrY (colour-blind). Overall, 2 out of 4 = 50% are colour-blind.
